text: Mecca LIVE: Eid-ul-Fitr Moon Sighting in Saudi, UAE | Holy Ramadan Month | Masjid al-Haram | N18GMecca Ramadan LIVE: Muslims Pray Tarweeh in the Grand Mosque of Mecca | Gulf News | Ramzan | CNBC TV18 Ramadan 2026 is expected to begin on or around February 17-18, 2026, and conclude with Eid al-Fitr on March 19 or 20, 2026, depending on the moon sighting. Saudi Arabia is likely to observe Eid on March 19 or 20, while South Asia (India/Pakistan) is expected to follow one day later on March 20 or 21, 2026. Eid ul-Fitr, also known as Ramzan Eid or Meethi Eid, marks the end of Ramadan, the holy month of fasting from dawn to sunset. The festival falls in the first three days of Shawwal in the Hijri calendar. Since moon visibility depends on location and atmospheric conditions, Eid is often celebrated on different days across countries. The Saudi Supreme Court has called on Muslims across the Kingdom to sight the crescent moon of Shawwal on the evening of Wednesday, March 18, marking the conclusion of Ramadan. In Turkey, Eid-Ul-Fitr will be celebrated on March 20. In Singapore, March 20 will mark the end of Ramzan and Eid will be celebrated on March 21. The month of Ramadan in India started on February 18, and today marks the 29th day of the holy month. According to the reports, the crescent moon will either be sighted on Thursday, March 19, or Friday, March 20. If the moon isn't sighted on March 19, the Muslims across the country will continue to fast until the moon is sighted.
